notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 5 of their last 7 games, including the last one. Keegan Kolesar takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Axel Sandin-Pellikka is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Johansson and Chiarot.
J.T. Compher is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games.
Simon Edvinsson has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. Albert Johansson has taken his spot beside Moritz Seider.
Cale Fleury has not dressed for the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Brandon Montour is out (lower body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-four defenseman.
Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 39% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, up from 2% last season.

SEA.head: The Kraken start a half-step behind
SEA.body: Even though Seattle has home-ice advantage, Detroit has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Kraken’s best way to tip it is keeping dangerous shots away.

DET.head: The Red Wings have a slight edge
DET.body: Even though Seattle has home-ice advantage, Detroit has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Kraken can still swing it if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: DeBrincat’s favorite opponent
paras: The Kraken won the first meeting this season, 6-3 in Detroit. The Red Wings come in at 2-3-2, the Kraken at 5-2-1.
The Red Wings’ power play has a soft target in the Kraken’s kill. The Kraken keep dangerous shots away, but the Wings give up a lot of them.

items.text: Alex DeBrincat has a point in at least seven straight games against Seattle.
